citations.field: PDF p. 96; printed p. 84; headword 听 yǐn; entry paragraph and adjacent boundary checked against supplied scan
citations.text: The 听 yǐn entry gives the received Shuowen analysis “从口，斤声” and the sense ‘smiling appearance’. It separately proposes a semantic explanation: because smiling opens the mouth, the graph is extended to ‘large mouth’; it cites Guangyun’s ‘口大貌’. The entry says that since the Yuan, 听 has also served as a simplified form of 聽, and calls this an “異代同形字” (same graphic form in different periods), distinguishing it from the yǐn word. This is the book author’s account, not proof of the proposed semantic mechanism or of the exact start of the 聽 spelling.

citations.source: 李學勤主編《字源》, 天津古籍出版社／遼寧人民出版社, 2012, ISBN 9787552800692; original scan inspected
citations.field: PDF pp. 1062–1063; printed pp. 1047–1048; 聽(听) entry, continuation verified in next column/page
citations.text: The 聽 entry identifies the oracle-bone and bronze forms as an associative construction from 耳 and 口, describing speech coming from the mouth and received by the ear; it says the 小篆 form’s 㥁 is an added sound marker. It reports oracle-bone uses for hearing and hearing/handling affairs, and bronze uses for obeying or accepting. The entry later states that 聽、聲、聖 share an origin and says 聽 is now simplified as 听. These are the book’s interpretations and cited examples; its reproduced historical glyphs are not independent artifact inspection in this research.

consulted_citations.text: Direct visual inspection confirms that the scan prints the headword readings as yǐn on the headword line and tīng on the following line. The provisional corpus OCR reverses these as ‘xī’ and ‘tīng’ on the preceding 唏 entry, then ‘yǐn’ as the 听 headword and a bare ‘tīng’; comparison with the pixels shows the line sequence at the 听 entry itself is yǐn then tīng. Proposed source-bound OCR correction: preserve ‘听 yǐn … / tīng’ for this entry and check the full page’s neighboring OCR if repairing the record. Do not alter raw OCR in place.
